title: Kenya Targets 800,000 Tonnes of Sugar Production in 2026
desc: Kenya is targeting 800,000 tonnes of sugar production in 2026 as the government pushes to strengthen local supply and reduce reliance on imports.
content:
Kenya is on course to produce about 800,000 metric tonnes of sugar by the end of 2026, Agriculture Cabinet Secretary Mutahi Kagwe has said, signalling stronger domestic production in the country's sugar sector.

The projection comes as the government continues implementing measures aimed at increasing local sugar production and ensuring the country has enough sugar for domestic consumption. Kagwe said Kenya currently has sufficient sugar to meet local demand.

The expected production level would represent an important development for Kenya's sugar industry, which has for years faced challenges linked to low local production, dependence on imports and difficulties affecting sugarcane farmers and millers.

The government has increasingly placed emphasis on rebuilding the local sugar industry as part of efforts to improve food security and strengthen agricultural production. The current approach has also included tighter controls on sugar imports as authorities seek to give local producers greater room to supply the domestic market.

For consumers, higher local production could help improve the consistency of sugar supplies if the projected output is achieved. It could also reduce pressure on the country to depend heavily on imported sugar to bridge gaps in domestic supply.

For farmers, stronger production creates the possibility of increased demand for sugarcane, although the benefits will depend on how effectively the sector addresses longstanding concerns around cane supply, miller efficiency and payments to farmers.

Kagwe's latest projection therefore places the focus not only on the amount of sugar Kenya can produce, but also on whether reforms in the sugar sector can translate into a more reliable industry for farmers, millers and consumers.

The 800,000-tonne target for 2026 will now be an important measure of the government's efforts to revive Kenya's sugar production and strengthen domestic supply.
